//: Type-checks packages/runtime, which `npm run typecheck` otherwise misses entirely (#341). The root tsconfig includes only src/**/*, and build:packages compiles seven packages of which runtime is not one — it is built separately by tsconfig.build.json inside `npm run build`. So runtime code that does not compile could pass typecheck, which it did twice (a BusinessError left without its `code` argument, caught two steps later by build).
//paths: Deliberately NOT extending tsconfig.build.json. That config sets "paths": {} so it resolves @falese/smt-contracts through node_modules to built dist, which would make typecheck depend on a prior build:packages. Inheriting the root paths instead checks runtime source against contracts SOURCE — no build required, and a contracts change is checked against runtime before anything is rebuilt, which is the direction breakage actually travels.
//rootDir: Anchored at the repo root, not packages/runtime/src. Inheriting the root paths pulls contracts source into the program, and the inherited rootDir (the repo's own src/) contains neither — either way tsc raises TS6059. Nothing is emitted here, so rootDir has no job beyond satisfying that check.
//exclude: Mirrors tsconfig.build.json. The gap this closes is that `build` compiles runtime source and `typecheck` did not, so this gate covers exactly what `build` covers. Runtime TESTS are type-checked by nothing today — ts-jest runs with isolatedModules, which transpiles without checking — and adding them here surfaces a large backlog of pre-existing errors in test fixtures. That is a real finding and a separate piece of work; see the note on #341.
